target.title: fix: OAuth refresh failures report reauth instead of stale success
target.body:
Closes #99120

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users with managed OpenAI OAuth profiles could see auth appear healthy after a refresh failure when an external Codex CLI credential still existed but was stale or invalidated. This made operator status false-green and could require repeated pairing-code relogs.

## Why This Change Was Made

The OAuth manager now fails closed on refresh errors instead of falling back to external CLI credentials after refresh failure. External CLI credentials remain available only for the existing unusable-profile bootstrap path.

Provider-wide auth discovery now also enforces that same ownership boundary: bootstrap-only Codex CLI `openai:default` is not synthesized as an automatic sibling candidate when a canonical local OpenAI OAuth profile already exists, unless that external profile was explicitly selected/configured.

Doctor and failed-turn refresh-failure hints include the affected safe profile id without mutating model defaults.

This touches CODEOWNERS auth files and likely needs auth/secops review.

## User Impact

Users and operators get an explicit reauth-required error for the affected profile instead of a misleading successful auth state. Doctor output and failed-turn guidance can point at the exact profile to relog without changing the user's default model.

## Review Response

Addressed the P1 review finding from `fuller-stack-dev` on head `66e088aff75f6727dc2c1754007d963fdceb6ad0`:

- `external-cli-sync.ts` no longer synthesizes runtime-only Codex CLI `openai:default` beside a named local OpenAI OAuth profile in provider-wide discovery.
- `resolveApiKeyForProvider` preserves the first typed `OAuthRefreshFailureError` while trying auth candidates and throws it when no earlier env/custom/synthetic fallback succeeds.
- `OAuthRefreshFailureError` carries a sanitized provider-prefixed `profileId`; `OAuthManagerRefreshError` passes it through with an explicit `override`.
- Failed-turn guidance now includes `--profile-id` for typed refresh failures.
- `docs/concepts/oauth.md` no longer documents runtime external CLI fallback after local Codex refresh failure.

The provider-wide regression was first run red before this commit: with expired `openai:user@example.com`, stale future-expiry Codex CLI credential, and no explicit profile lock, `resolveApiKeyForProvider({ provider: "openai" })` returned `profile:openai:default`. It now rejects with the OAuth refresh failure and does not persist the Codex CLI token.

Live customer/setup evidence for the original false-green behavior is in #99120. I did not replay a live customer credential against this branch; the post-fix proof is the deterministic provider-wide regression plus focused type/test validation below.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/auth-profiles/oauth.openai-codex-refresh-fallback.test.ts`: 1 Vitest shard, 20 tests passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/auth-profiles/oauth-refresh-failure.test.ts src/agents/auth-profiles.external-cli-sync.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-execution.test.ts src/agents/auth-profiles/oauth.openai-codex-refresh-fallback.test.ts src/commands/doctor-auth.hints.test.ts`: 4 Vitest shards, 277 tests passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`: passed.
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 <touched auth/reply files>`: passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local --base origin/main --prompt <auth refresh fallback scope>`: first Codex-engine run surfaced one P1 (`OAuthManagerRefreshError.profileId` needed `override` after adding the base property); fixed in this PR and proven by `pnpm tsgo:core`. A second Codex-engine rerun stalled with heartbeat-only output and returned only a wrapper `KeyboardInterrupt` trace when interrupted. Claude-engine fallback failed due local Claude connector/auth precedence, not code.
